tasks.short: Nominate citizens to boards or commissions through eligibility checks, conversations and formal approval.

steps.what: Confirm the vacancy, nomination powers and appointment criteria.
Collect candidate profiles, declarations and missing information.
Check eligibility and identify conflicts requiring interpretation.
Discuss suitability, availability and willingness with candidates.
Compare candidates and document the proposed nomination.
Approve the nomination under the applicable delegation.
Send the approved nomination to the appointing authority.

tasks.design: Configure a nomination register and intake form in the {WORKFLOW}, with controlled dossiers in the {DOCS}. Explicit rules flag missing information and eligibility exceptions; people assess conflicts and suitability, while approved notices pass through the {EMAIL} after a release check.
tasks.previous_blocker: Infrequent appointments, differing mandates and scattered correspondence made bespoke automation unattractive. Suitability remained a personal governance judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forms, document templates and approval routing can handle the administration. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of connecting these components without automating candidate selection.
tasks.still_hard: Informal candidate networks, contested conflicts and legitimacy cannot be reduced to eligibility fields. National appointment rules and the distinction between nomination and appointment need careful interpretation.
tasks.human_edge: Judge independence, public trust and the contribution a candidate would make to the whole board.

ambition.what: Offer first-time citizen candidates an accessible nomination route with clear requirements.

tasks.altitude: The chief executive spends less time chasing dossiers and more time discussing independence and board needs. Nomination and appointment rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Coordinate induction for newly appointed board or commission members.
reach.learn: Learn governance boundaries, induction needs and how to track readiness without assessing political suitability.

evidence.claim: Forms, explicit eligibility checks, document templates and approval routing can support nomination administration.
The GDPR restricts solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects on individuals.

assumptions: This supplemental task applies to public bodies or organisations with citizen nomination duties; it is unusual in an ordinary private company.
The example requires governing-body approval; another lawful delegation may place approval with the chief executive.
Routine collection moves to structured submissions; disputed eligibility and conflicts still receive human assessment.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured savings.
The access range includes privacy review and any consultation required by national rules. GDPR and applicable EU AI Act duties remain relevant.
unknowns: Whether the organisation has any citizen nomination duty.
Who may nominate, approve and appoint.
Which eligibility and conflict rules are explicit enough to encode.
Which intake, access and retention controls are already available.
research_questions: Which appointment requirements can be checked mechanically, and which require legal interpretation?
Would an open application route reach suitable candidates outside existing networks?
new_work: Resolve incomplete submissions and disputed eligibility flags.
Maintain appointment criteria, delegations and notice templates.
Review dossier access and apply retention rules.
Check the recipient and approved version before releasing each nomination.

tasks.short: Direct sensitive investigations, resolve complaints and give evidence at hearings.

steps.what: Assess the complaint, urgency, conflicts and investigation mandate.
Preserve relevant records and restrict access to authorised investigators.
Read evidence and prepare a chronology with unresolved questions.

loop.input: Only authorised preserved evidence, with stable record and page identifiers.
loop.output: A draft chronology, source-linked statements and unresolved questions; allegations remain labelled as allegations.
loop.check: Validate every reference mechanically; the investigator checks dates, quotations, contradictions and omitted context against originals.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass per evidence batch; unresolved statements enter a manual review queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text accounts describe events inconsistently. Templates cannot extract their meaning or distinguish competing accounts.

steps.what: Conduct interviews or hearings and test conflicting accounts.
Evaluate findings and decide a lawful response within delegated powers.
Give personal testimony and answer questions at an external hearing.
Record remediation owners, deadlines and follow-up requirements.

tasks.design: Configure restricted case records and evidence preservation in the {DOCS}, with authorised collection from the {EMAIL}. A bounded extraction loop proposes a source-linked chronology for investigator review; approved remediation becomes tracked work in the {PROJECT}. Interviews, findings and testimony remain personal responsibilities.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence sits across correspondence and documents, while preservation, privilege and access requirements discourage informal tools. Earlier automation could organise records but struggled with inconsistent witness narratives.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing retention and case permissions can support controlled collection. Bounded extraction can prepare a chronology when every statement remains traceable to preserved evidence.
tasks.still_hard: Credibility, procedural fairness, privilege and protection against retaliation require expert judgement. Access mistakes or misleading summaries can compromise an investigation.
tasks.human_edge: Listen fairly, challenge conflicting evidence and accept responsibility for decisions and truthful testimony.

ambition.what: Provide an anonymised remediation review that identifies recurring process failures across closed cases.

tasks.altitude: The chief executive receives better organised evidence and clearer remediation follow-up, while most investigation time remains human. No new authority over findings, sanctions or testimony is created.

reach.task: Verify that operational remediation fixes the failure identified by an investigation.
reach.learn: Learn evidence-based closure, confidentiality boundaries and how to distinguish completed actions from effective remedies.

evidence.claim: Restricted evidence registers, preservation controls and remediation tracking are established deterministic capabilities.
Source-referenced answers with staff checking are demonstrated in a public-sector rules application; this does not validate investigation summaries.
A documented AI-assisted government report contained fabricated references and a fabricated court case, supporting direct source verification.
The GDPR restricts solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects on individuals.

assumptions: This is exceptional executive involvement in serious cases, rather than routine handling of every complaint.
The example combines an investigation with a later hearing; testimony does not occur in every case.
An independent investigator or governing body takes over when the chief executive has a conflict.
Preserved originals remain authoritative; model outputs never become witness evidence.
Time shares and build ranges are estimates for a controlled pilot.
The access range includes confidentiality, privacy and any consultation required by national rules. GDPR and applicable EU AI Act duties apply.
unknowns: Which complaint types reach the chief executive.
Who may preserve evidence, decide findings and impose remedies.
Whether current retention controls support legal holds and restricted case access.
Whether cases contain special-category data, privileged material or protected disclosures.
Which national hearing and employee consultation rules apply.
research_questions: Can reviewers detect omitted context and contradictions as reliably as incorrect quotations?
Which evidence categories should be excluded from model processing entirely?
Can closed-case lessons be anonymised without exposing complainants or witnesses?
new_work: Check extracted chronology entries against original evidence.
Handle unreadable records, contradictory dates and missing references.
Review case access, preservation and retention exceptions.
Maintain extraction instructions and evaluate them on representative closed cases.
Check remediation effectiveness and anonymise cross-case lessons.

tasks.short: Direct investment-product or financial-service operations through performance review, executive decisions and controlled implementation.

steps.what: Retrieve trading, service and exposure reports from the regulated financial operations system {OTHER}.
Reconcile operational performance with revenue, costs and agreed reporting definitions.
Review the management pack and identify matters requiring executive discussion.

loop.input: Reconciled figures, approved metric definitions, business commentary and the current risk report.
loop.output: A discussion brief with source-linked variances, reported explanations and explicit unresolved questions.
loop.check: Check all figures against the reconciled dataset; the chief executive reviews context and separates reported explanations from established causes.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass per reporting cycle; missing or inconsistent data produces an exception notice.
loop.why_not_simpler: Deterministic rules identify numerical changes, but cannot condense varied business commentary into useful discussion questions.

steps.what: Set priorities, resolve business trade-offs and agree proposed operating changes.
Review regulatory implications and approve changes within the delegated mandate.
Translate the approved decision into instructions, owners and deadlines.
Refresh performance tracking and flag missed implementation milestones.

tasks.design: Connect the regulated financial operations system {OTHER} and the {ERP} through governed reconciliation jobs in the {DATA_PLATFORM}, feeding the {BI}. A bounded loop drafts discussion points from verified figures and management commentary. Executives and control functions approve operating changes before the {WORKFLOW} creates implementation records in the {PROJECT}; the solution has no trading authority.
tasks.previous_blocker: Operational and finance reports use different definitions and cut-off times. The main barrier was reliable reconciliation and ownership of metrics, rather than a lack of narrative generation.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing interfaces, planning controls and dashboards can support a shared reporting layer. AI-assisted coding can reduce connector and reconciliation development effort; a small model loop can prepare commentary.
tasks.still_hard: Valuation, exposure definitions, regulatory interpretation and conflicting commercial incentives remain difficult. Executive direction must respect independent control functions and delegated limits.
tasks.human_edge: Balance customer outcomes, risk capacity and commercial priorities, then hold business leaders accountable for the trade-offs.

ambition.what: Review service-capacity bottlenecks weekly using reconciled demand, margin and risk information.

tasks.altitude: The chief executive spends less review time establishing which figures agree and more time challenging proposed actions. Decision rights remain within existing mandates; operational managers gain clearer implementation ownership.

reach.task: Turn executive operating decisions into capacity plans and verified delivery milestones.
reach.learn: Learn service economics, risk escalation thresholds and how to measure whether a change improved customer outcomes.

evidence.claim: Report summarisation and data questions are existing capabilities, but depend on prepared data models.
Planning software can draft narratives about assumptions and risks; this supports preparation rather than executive authority.
A vendor case reports reduced executive reporting effort; its method is not given and does not establish equivalent savings here.
Reconciliation, approval routing and milestone tracking can be deterministic; investment-business direction remains human.

assumptions: This task applies to an organisation providing investment products or financial services, rather than an ordinary company's treasury activity.
The regulated financial operations system is represented by {OTHER}; existing finance and reporting capabilities are reused where available.
The chief executive approves within delegation after control-function review; reserved matters escalate to the governing body.
Implementation templates cover routine operating changes; unusual instructions are written manually.
Time shares and build ranges are estimates for a limited reporting and implementation scope.
The access range includes regulated-data permissions, privacy assessment and consultation under national rules where applicable. GDPR and applicable EU AI Act duties apply.
The solution does not score natural persons for credit, monitor individual staff performance or execute transactions.
unknowns: Which regulated activities and permissions the organisation holds.
Which systems contain transactions, exposures, service activity and authoritative valuations.
Whether reporting interfaces and approved metric definitions exist.
Which decisions require independent control-function or governing-body approval.
How much reporting preparation is performed by analysts rather than the chief executive.
research_questions: Which reconciliation breaks cause executive decisions to be delayed?
Can existing reporting configuration deliver the required views before custom connectors are built?
Which management explanations need challenge rather than summarisation?
new_work: Investigate reconciliation breaks and stale source feeds.
Review generated discussion points for unsupported causal claims.
Maintain metric definitions, risk limits and approval delegations.
Handle implementation exceptions and verify outcomes.
Review access and connector changes with control functions.

tasks.short: Prepare bylaws for elected approval and oversee their lawful implementation and enforcement.

steps.what: Confirm legal powers, policy intent and the required adoption procedure.
Draft the bylaw and its explanatory memorandum.

loop.input: Approved policy instructions, verified legislation, current bylaw and approved clauses with version identifiers.
loop.output: A marked-up draft, explanatory memorandum and explicit list of unresolved drafting questions.
loop.check: Check references and clause provenance mechanically; legal counsel checks meaning, powers, omissions and consistency before circulation.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass per instructed revision; unresolved legal questions return to legal counsel without invented wording or sources.
loop.why_not_simpler: Clause assembly handles standard wording, but reconciling policy instructions with varied existing text needs bounded language drafting.

steps.what: Discuss the proposal with affected parties and resolve policy concerns.
Review legality, procedural compliance and the final adoption text.
Debate amendments and vote on the bylaw.
Publish the adopted text and its effective date through the required official channel.
Assign implementation responsibilities, resources and escalation routes.
Collect implementation returns and assemble overdue obligations.
Review serious enforcement exceptions and direct action within lawful powers.

tasks.design: Use controlled templates and clause versions in the {DOCS}, with a bounded loop preparing drafts for legal review. The {WORKFLOW} records consultation, adoption and publication checks, then stages the approved text for the {GOV_PORTAL}. Implementation records in the {PROJECT} feed compliance reporting, while elected approval and enforcement judgements remain human.
tasks.previous_blocker: Legal drafting, consultation and elected decisions were treated as one indivisible task. Version control and publication requirements also varied across authorities.
tasks.enabler_now: Document controls, approval workflows and clause libraries already cover much of the administration. Bounded drafting can assist with instructed revisions while preserving source references and legal review.
tasks.still_hard: Legal powers, proportionality, consultation duties and amendments require expert judgement. National rules determine valid adoption, publication, commencement and enforcement.
tasks.human_edge: Translate public policy into lawful obligations, reconcile conflicting interests and defend proportionate enforcement.

ambition.what: Publish a reviewed plain-language implementation guide alongside each newly adopted bylaw.

tasks.altitude: The chief executive spends less time resolving document versions and chasing implementation returns. Elected officials retain adoption authority, and enforcement powers do not expand.

reach.task: Translate adopted obligations into practical procedures and evidence of implementation.
reach.learn: Learn commencement rules, operational feasibility and when an implementation question needs legal interpretation.

evidence.claim: Controlled templates, clause assembly, version comparison and obligation reminders can be deterministic.
A public-sector application provides source-referenced explanations of planning rules for staff checking; this is narrower than drafting valid bylaws.
Structured governance-paper drafting from management documents is available, but does not establish legal drafting accuracy.
The EU AI Act includes an editorial-review exception to disclosure requirements for certain AI-generated public-interest text.

assumptions: This supplemental task belongs to a public body with elected approval powers. It is not typical work in a private mid-size company.
Corporate governance policies would be a separate adaptation; they are not treated as statutory bylaws here.
The example uses an official publication route through the {GOV_PORTAL}; the required channel depends on national rules.
Publication automation requires a supported interface or approved submission mechanism; otherwise a person submits the prepared package.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates. They exclude elapsed consultation, legislative deliberation and election timetables.
The access range includes privacy assessment and employee consultation where implementation changes trigger national rules. GDPR and applicable EU AI Act duties apply.
A person reviews public-facing text and holds editorial responsibility; legal counsel checks applicable disclosure requirements.
unknowns: Whether the organisation has bylaw-making or enforcement powers.
Which elected body approves and which amendments require renewed review.
Which national adoption, consultation and publication rules apply.
Whether approved clauses and current legislation are maintained with reliable versions.
Whether the official publication channel supports integration.
Which enforcement powers are delegated to the chief executive.
research_questions: Which drafting changes can use approved clauses without changing their legal effect?
How can the adopted version be verified against the published version and effective date?
Which implementation indicators reveal practical enforcement problems without prejudging individual cases?
new_work: Maintain verified legislation, clause versions and adoption templates.
Review draft wording and repair unsupported references.
Check the exact adopted text, publication acknowledgement and effective date.
Maintain obligation owners and investigate missing compliance returns.
Review plain-language guides for consistency with authoritative text.

role.altitude: The chief executive gains better prepared evidence, clearer records and more reliable follow-up. Nomination, investigation, regulated-business direction and bylaw decisions remain bounded by existing delegations and public or board accountability.
reach: Work with the general and operations manager to turn approved decisions into procedures, milestones and verified outcomes.
Build shared reporting definitions with finance and control functions before requesting automated commentary.
Use governance and legal specialists to distinguish administrative checks from decisions requiring independent judgement.
skills_to_grow: Specify decision rights and approval points precisely.
Challenge source quality, missing context and unsupported causal claims.
Design proportionate access, retention and exception handling.
Evaluate implementation through outcomes rather than completed paperwork.
Understand applicable GDPR, EU AI Act and national procedural requirements.
role.ambitious_version: Run a shorter cycle from verified evidence to accountable decisions and tested implementation, while using the recovered preparation time to hear unfamiliar candidates, affected parties and operational concerns.
